# libsodium

[libsodium.org](https://libsodium.org) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/libsodium](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/libsodium)

**Status: available.** 8 of OSS-Fuzz's 8 fuzz targets have statements. 32 binaries, 15 MB. 118 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 118 open.

Built from libsodium (commit `2c61b499`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [crypto_aead_fuzzer](crypto_aead_fuzzer/) | Checks one property, a round trip: AEAD round trip for an input-chosen primitive (chacha20poly1305 ietf/original, xchacha20poly1305, aegis128l, aegis256, aes256gcm) with input key, nonce, message and AD: decrypt(encrypt(m, ad)) has length msg_len and equals m byte for byte -- but ONLY if decrypt returned 0; a decrypt that rejects its own ciphertext is not caught. | none | 15 |
| [crypto_box_fuzzer](crypto_box_fuzzer/) | Checks 3 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: crypto_box_open_easy(crypto_box_easy(m)) must succeed and reproduce m exactly (message from input, nonce from input, keypair 1 from an input seed, keypair 2 from the input-seeded deterministic RNG). | 1 check (api-contract; all confirmed in the binary) | 15 |
| [crypto_generichash_fuzzer](crypto_generichash_fuzzer/) | Computes BLAKE2b with the one-shot crypto_generichash and again with init/update(two halves)/final into the SAME buffer `out`; the two digests are never compared (a ready-made one-shot vs streaming differential that is not checked). | none | 15 |
| [crypto_kdf_fuzzer](crypto_kdf_fuzzer/) | crypto_kdf_derive_from_key with input key, subkey id, context and length; the subkey and return code are ignored. | none | 15 |
| [crypto_kx_fuzzer](crypto_kx_fuzzer/) | Seed keypair, then client and server session keys against an input public key; returns and keys ignored. The natural law (client rx == server tx and vice versa for a matched pair) is not checked -- the harness even reuses the same keypair for both roles and overwrites rx/tx. | none | 15 |
| [crypto_sign_fuzzer](crypto_sign_fuzzer/) | Checks 3 properties (listed below); the first, a self-validation: An Ed25519 detached signature just made over the input message with an input-seeded key must verify under the matching public key. | 2 checks (self-validation; all confirmed in the binary) | 15 |
| [secret_key_auth_fuzzer](secret_key_auth_fuzzer/) | Checks one property, a self-validation: crypto_auth (HMAC-SHA512-256) of the whole input under a deterministic-RNG key must pass crypto_auth_verify with the same key. | 1 check (self-validation; all confirmed in the binary) | 15 |
| [secretbox_easy_fuzzer](secretbox_easy_fuzzer/) | No summary of this harness is recorded yet; its checks, if any, are listed below. | none | 13 |

Not included: **api-driver** (held from this release).

## What the statements say, for libsodium
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

The harnesses with a check whose failure ends the process with a status that a halts statement excludes, so that a proof of that statement implies the check on every input it covers:
- `crypto_box_fuzzer`: crypto_box_easy must return 0 on every input.
- `crypto_sign_fuzzer`: an Ed25519 detached signature just made over the input message with an input-seeded key must verify under the matching public key; multi-part (Ed25519ph) signature built with init/update(two halves)/final_create must verify with a fresh init/update(same halves)/final_verify.
- `secret_key_auth_fuzzer`: crypto_auth (HMAC-SHA512-256) of the whole input under a deterministic-RNG key must pass crypto_auth_verify with the same key.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch libsodium
    ./oft verify-sha libsodium

By hand: download `libsodium-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/libsodium/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [jedisct1/libsodium](https://github.com/jedisct1/libsodium) at `2c61b499e7cea2d873a9afee220c946601f78beb`, built with autotools
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
